title: Localization descent for the derived signed shift equation
statement:
theorem derived_shift_descent {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso g]
    [∀ x : X, Invertible (l : X.residueField x)]
    [∀ y : Y, Invertible (l : Y.residueField y)]
    [EssentiallySmall.{u + 1} X.ProEt] [EssentiallySmall.{u + 1} Y.ProEt] (s : Option ℕ)
    (SX : Closed l E X s) (SY : Closed l E Y s)
    (TX : Models l E X s SX) (TY : Models l E Y s SY)
    (c : Comparison l E g s SX SY TX TY)
    (hmodel : ∀ (P I : K l E Y s) (hI : I.IsKInjective) (a b : ℤ),
      derivedShiftEquation l E g s SX SY TX TY c
        ((podReindexingQ l E Y s).obj P)
        ((podReindexingQ l E Y s).obj I) a b) :
    ∀ (M N : podReindexingDerived l E Y s) (a b : ℤ),
      derivedShiftEquation l E g s SX SY TX TY c M N a b

source.place: Step 4; localization descent sub-obligation extracted from lem-pod-reindexing-shift-derived-part.

proof.text: The recorded derived category uses HasDerivedCategory.standard. The object bijection Localization.Construction.objEquiv for quasi-isomorphisms therefore writes every source literally as Q(P), without transporting along a source isomorphism. Fix P and integers a,b. Curry the derived Hom functors in their second variable. The signedShift components are the components of a natural isomorphism: whisker sourceShift.symm by shift b, then whisker the normalized target commShiftIso b by shift -a, then compose with shiftFunctorAdd' for b+(-a)=b-a.

Use the Grothendieck abelianness projection of the independent-universe ringed-site resolution theorem to obtain K-injective resolutions. DerivedCategory.exists_iso_Q_obj_of_isKInjective supplies a K-injective I and an isomorphism N ≅ Q(I).

At the fixed source, curry the natural comparison c.derived. Package the left-hand side as a composite of this comparison at M[a], the map induced by the inverse source commShiftIso, the target commShiftIso, and signedShiftNat at F(M). Package the right-hand side as signedShiftNat at M followed by the output commShiftIso and the shifted comparison at M. Componentwise functoriality identifies these with the two sides of derivedShiftEquation. The supplied hmodel gives equality at Q(I). Naturality along N ≅ Q(I) and cancellation of the induced target isomorphism give equality at N. No representative equation is re-proved or assumed under a new name.

proof_origin.place: Step 4, localization descent; R9 proof via the standard localization object bijection, naturality only in the target, and cancellation along a K-injective resolution isomorphism.
